entities.summary: Ailsa Craig is an island of 99 ha in the outer Firth of Clyde, 16 km west of mainland Scotland. The island's microgranite has long been quarried to make curling stones. The now-uninhabited island comprises an eroded magmatic pluton formed during the same period of igneous activity as magmatic rocks on the nearby Isle of Arran.
